artifacts: A kettle caught mid-pour, the water standing in the air from spout to cup like a piece of blown glass. The cup below is still warm, and it has been waiting three years for the pour to finish.
A handprint pressed into solid stone at door-height, fingers too long by one and the palm narrow. The stone has healed at its edges, the way ice closes over a stone.
A child's marble, clear glass with a spiral of blue deep inside it. Held up to the light, the spiral turns on its own, slowly, the way something far away would.
A pair of reading glasses with one lens crazed along lines no impact could have made. Through the cracked lens, distances read wrong, and they read wrong consistently.
A field notebook swollen with water, every page legible except one, where the ink lifted and left a faint square. Someone pressed a photograph there and took it back.
A wool glove with the initial M inked inside the cuff. It lies on open ground, and the ground under it is dry, and stays dry whatever the weather does.
A brass key with no ward and no bit, smooth as a tongue. It opens nothing here, and yet something somewhere keeps clicking whenever it is carried past a wall.
A coffee mug ringed with old use, a thumbprint worn into the handle on the left side. It still tastes of coffee if you drink from it, of whatever it holds.
A tape recorder with one reel left on it. Her voice counts a shift in fours, and under the count, faint as a room tone, something is breathing along.
A sealed envelope stamped and addressed to a name that worked at this station years before you were born. The postmark is dated a month after that person died.
A steel thermos left open, its soup still hot, steam rising in the cold. It tastes of a summer that never once reached the ridge, and you drink anyway.
A spiral of flat stones stacked without mortar, each one placed a hand's turn from the last. Grass between the joints is cut clean, green, and no goat has ever climbed this high.
Six parallel furrows gouged in a rock face, each one as long as your arm, the stone at the bottom of them faintly warm. Nothing this wide drags itself up a cliff face, and this happened recently.

A pair of boot prints that begin in the middle of a bare slab and end in the middle of the same slab, stepping sideways through solid rock. The prints are fresh, and they are a size you have measured on your own feet.
